title: I was thrilled when Amandaland started filming on my street…  but when I saw the first episode I nearly spat out my wine: HARRY WALLOP reveals why having a BBC crew on his doorstep was more hit job than hit series
text:
In September of last year, some filming in our street in Highbury, north of London, were carried out. This is not unusual for a couple of reasons. The first is practical: the street where I live is a particularly quiet route thanks to a complex unidirectional system; Almost no car leads for him, which makes him ideal for a quiet filming and without disturbances.
The second: I am surrounded by the types of Luvvie of the media, such as me, of the guy who let the filming teams enter their homes in exchange for a little extra cash or the possibility of showing their elegant cooking islands before Put your market properties.
We have made Itv film some of its identifiers (the mini films to which they are transmitted to announce their own channel) on our street; Rosamund Pike (a place) has filmed a Hollywood movie just around the corner and I can barely appear in the stores without running with Paul Mescal to run, showing his gladiator II with perfected pests.
So I did not step on a eyelid when a crew, with centers that accompany it for the restoration, a trailer with portaloos and men with rolls of adhesive tape, installed in our path. Walking the dog, an educated corridor asked if he could wait a minute so as not to ruin the scene that was filmed. I asked what the show was. “Well, I’m not destined to tell you,” he said, “but when I’m causing an inconvenience, I will. I saw actress Lucy Punch with Joanna Lumley preparing for her scene.
In the photo: Lucy Punch (left) and Joanna Lumley (right), stars of the BBC Amandaland series
In the photo: the cast and the team meet as the filming is carried out in highbury, north of London
I could not get home quickly enough to tell my 16 -year -old daughter, Celia, who was hysterical emotion. Are you kidding? In our street? She screamed. Motherland is one of his favorite programs and the monstrous and Snobby Amanda, as many fans will attest, the best character. To think that our lovely Oasis of Islington was chosen as their surroundings. Obviously, the writers had decided that Amanda needed to leave a chiswick in western London and travel north where there are better restaurants, more elegant delicatessos and, frankly, a set of more elegant people. This has always been an area where lawyers (we are at a short distance from the inns of the Court) have chosen to live, where the novelists rub their shoulders with television directors and where they run into Nigel Slater in the local butcher.
Except that, as we all hurry to see the filming of rubber neck, we notice something strange. The production team had left a tip shop in the pavement; The garbage had spread outside Amanda’s floor. What was happening?
Then I saw that the house they had chosen as Amanda’s new abode was, well, one of the most disarrking of the street. Still very pleasant, and it is probably worth 1.6 million that an average house in the N5 Highbury postal code obtains, but they need a lick of paint.
The BBC press release, announcing the program, exposed the complete horror: “After its divorce, Amanda has had to reduce the size and sticks to South Harlesden, or as the real estate agent calls it soha.” Then, Mother Alfa has fallen into difficult times and the location explorers thought that our street, with an ingenious outgoing, was descending enough to defend themselves from the area around the Wormwood prison.
In the photo: Amandaland filming in highbury, north of London – Lucy Punch passes from the yellow truck
In the photo: the production equipment leaves a shopping cart on the pavement
Excuse me! But that is an insult in the good name of Highbury, a London area with cinnamon rolls and more expensive cut coffees than Notting Hill, frankly.
I almost spit my wine when I saw in the first episode that Amanda’s mother, played by Joanna Lumley, comes with a “small Waitrose tuck package, now that you only have one meter of Tesco.” That?! Highbury’s main supermarket * is * a waitrose, although some of us bought in the delicatessen of ridiculously expensive performance at the end of the road, which sells biodynamic wines and those delicious chickpeas provided by Navarric Brindisa. Or we appear in the Ottolenghi, a few steps away in Upper Street.
Are we as elegant as Chelsea? No. Do the properties get as much as Belgravia? Anywhere near. But this is one of the most beautiful corners in London, whatever Amandaland can suggest.
However, the game of hands when it comes to the location does not decrease from a very acute writing. Amanda may have suffered a messy divorce and collapse in the circumstances, but she is still very funny.
